# Thermostat Guide

## Changing the schedule

The thermostat follows a weekly schedule of up to four periods per day. To change a period, open the schedule screen, tap the day, and drag the period's start time; the thermostat applies the change the next time that period begins. A temporary hold overrides the schedule until the next period and is cleared when the next period starts. Every change is confirmed with a short click from the thermostat's speaker, and the display shows the updated schedule for a few minutes before returning to the temperature screen. If nobody has changed the schedule and the periods look different, check whether the thermostat's clock drifted after a power cut.

## Button sounds

Each press of a button on the thermostat is confirmed with a click. The click can be turned off in the sound settings, and the thermostat then confirms a press by briefly brightening the display instead. Turning the click off does not affect the heating or cooling equipment and does not change the schedule. The thermostat also makes a soft click every few minutes while the screen is off; this is the backlight relay and is normal.

## Troubleshooting the equipment

### Short cycling

The furnace runs for a brief period, stops, and starts again repeatedly without reaching the set temperature. The usual causes are a clogged air filter, which lets the burner reach its high-limit switch quickly, a blocked flue or supply register, or equipment that is oversized for the space. Replace the filter, open every register, and have the installer check the equipment sizing. The thermostat's own settings are rarely the cause.

### No heat at all

Check that the system switch is set to heat, that the set temperature is above the room temperature, and that the furnace's power switch and the breaker are on. If the furnace has a pilot light, follow the lighting instructions on the furnace.
